title: feat(ref): flag .ref(by) where the class declares no static by
description:
## .what

a lint rule (or a type-level guard) that flags `X.contract().ref('<by>')` where the domain object
`X` declares no `static <by>` (e.g. `.ref('primary')` on a class with no `public static primary`).

## .why

`.ref(by)` throws `ConstraintError … requires static <by>` when the dobj declares no such key. a
handler's schema is a module-level const, so the throw lands at import: a cold-start crash on
deploy, never a 400 and never a test failure until the module loads.

declapract-typescript-ehmpathy carried this as a bad-practice check (#634, #565). it is a property
of the domain-objects api, not of a repo's practice set, so it belongs with domain-objects:

- a lint rule shipped beside the library reaches every consumer on install, with no declapract upgrade
- better still, a type that makes `.ref(by)` reject a `by` the class does not declare turns the
  cold-start crash into a compile error

## .shape of the fix

- preferred: type `.ref<B>(by: B)` so that `B` must be a declared static key of `X`
- fallback: a lint rule that reads the class's statics and flags an undeclared `by`
- in the error: name the class, the `by`, and the one-line fix
  (`public static primary = ['uuid'] as const;` where the dobj has a uuid)

source: ehmpathy/declapract-typescript-ehmpathy#634, #565
